title: ML-Based Cyber Kill Chain Classification for IoT Devices in SOHO Environments
content: Small office and home office networks are increasingly targeted by adversaries exploiting the growing population of IoT devices, yet most machine learning-based intrusion detection systems for IoT are limited to “attack classification” and provide little insight into where an intrusion sits within the broader attack lifecycle. This study develops a two-phase machine learning-based intrusion detection for small office and home office IoT traffic that extends conventional intrusion detection into “Cyber Kill Chain” stage classification and incorporates explainable AI to support transparent, actionable defences. Using the CICIoT2023 six-class dataset, Random Forest, Decision Tree and LightGBM were trained and evaluated. Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy while LightGBM offered a favourable trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency. LightGBM was used to classify detected intrusions into four Cyber Kill Chain stages, achieving near-perfect precision and recall for reconnaissance and delivery-stage traffic, but comparatively weaker performance for exploitation and command-and-control traffic. Feature importance and SHAP analysis identified inter-arrival time and flow duration as the dominant drivers of stage classification. These findings show that machine learning-based intrusion detection can combine high accuracy with stage-aware explainable contextualisation, offering a practical foundation for proactive defence strategies in small office and home office environments.
